connector: The boys are lost in the fog, and two strangers have grabbed them. Today you’ll meet those strangers up close. Listen for the names they call each other, and watch what happens every time the prince opens his mouth.

a.raw: cutwater was a thin man sharp as a knife blade and he moved like a shadow
a.fixed: Cutwater was a thin man, sharp as a knife blade, and he moved like a shadow.
a.why: Cutwater is a name, so it gets a capital. Commas go around the describing part, sharp as a knife blade. And joins the last part. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: billy was a big man loud as thunder and he smelled of garlic
b.fixed: Billy was a big man, loud as thunder, and he smelled of garlic.
b.why: Billy is a name, so it gets a capital. Commas go around the describing part, loud as thunder. And joins the last part. A period ends the sentence.

mfill1.h1: Say the two parts out loud, one right after the other.
mfill1.why: the part that means between, plus rupt (break): to break in between.

mfill2.h1: Put the first part in front of a word you already know.
mfill2.why: the part that means between, plus act: to act between people.

mfill3.h1: The second part is a whole word. Stick the first part on the front.
mfill3.why: the part that means between, plus national: between nations.

mfill4.h1: The second part has to do with the sea. Join them with no space.
mfill4.why: the part that means under, plus marine (sea): a boat that goes under the sea.

vcloze1.h1: Which word in the bank names a rough, cruel person?
vcloze1.why: a ruffian is a rough, violent person, a bully.

vcloze2.h1: Ballad sellers sing about daring deeds. Which bank word means that?
vcloze2.why: an exploit is a bold, daring act.

vcloze3.h1: Who gets the throne after the king? Find that word in the bank.
vcloze3.why: the heir is the person who will get a throne or title.

vcloze4.h1: The outlaws want money in exchange for the prince. Which bank word is that?
vcloze4.why: a ransom is money paid to free a prisoner.

gfill1.h1: Cold and hungry are two troubles that go together. Which word adds one to the other?

gfill2.h1: The lantern coming closer made them run. Which word shows a result?

gfill3.h1: Being scared and walking anyway push against each other.

gfill4.h1: Shouting at someone usually gets an answer. Did it here?
gfill4.why: but shows a difference: he shouted, yet Jemmy ignored him.

match.ruffian: A ruffian is a kind of person, a rough one. Look for the meaning about a bully or criminal.
match.exploit: An exploit is something someone does, the kind of thing people sing about. Look for the bold, daring act.
match.heir: An heir is the person next in line. Look for the meaning about getting a throne.
match.ransom: A ransom is money. Look for the meaning about paying to free a prisoner.

cards.title: The King’s Crest
cards.sub: What Cutwater sees on the saddle
cards.look: A dark night in the fog, and the saddle on the horse the boys rode from the castle. In Chapter 5, Cutwater holds his lantern up to the saddle and sees something important.
cards.todo: Do Step 1 to see what Cutwater saw. Step 2 is just for fun.
cards.step1p: Tap the lantern to hold it up to the saddle, the way Cutwater does.

art.alt: Part of an old red and gold royal flag with lions and a crown
art.title: Royal Standard of Great Britain (detail)
art.creator: Unknown maker

revealText: This is part of a real king’s flag, hand-painted about 200 years ago. The lions and the crown are the king’s family signs. A family’s special picture like this is called a crest.
The saddle in the story carries the king’s crest. That is how the outlaws figure out the horse came from the king’s own castle.
cards.step2p: A crest tells people who your family is. Tap a color, tap a picture, and type one word that is true about you.

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Opti. Our runaways are in real trouble now. Two rough men have found them in the fog, and one of the boys can’t seem to stop talking. Today, think about this: when you’re in danger, is it smarter to stay quiet or to speak up? Watch what each boy chooses.
transcripts.guide1: Today the word work asks you to use what you’ve learned. You’ll build words from their parts, fill in sentences with this week’s vocabulary, and join short sentences with the right joining word. Before you type, read each sentence in your head. Your ears often know the answer before your eyes do.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read Chapter 5, a tip: notice the moment Jemmy uses his elbow instead of his voice. Authors often show what a character is thinking through what they do. And when the lantern comes close to the saddle, slow down. One small thing changes everything.
transcripts.guide3: Today your opinion gets proof. A text example is a moment from the book that shows your reason is true, and you always say which chapter it came from. Go back to a chapter, find the moment, and tell what happened in your own words.
transcripts.card-crest: Look closely at a king’s things, and you’ll often find his family’s signs, like lions and crowns. When the outlaws spot the king’s crest on the saddle, they know where that horse came from. Now it’s your turn. Design a crest that tells the world something about you.

notes.wordParts: inter- means “between” (interrupt, interact, international). sub- means “under” (submarine).
notes.grammar: A conjunction is a joining word. and adds an idea, but shows a difference, and so shows a result.
notes.spelling: A vowel team is two vowels that make one sound, like ai in rain. A team stays together in one syllable: rain·bow, sea·son.
notes.wgrd: Good readers notice how characters handle pressure: who keeps calm, who keeps talking, and why.
vocab: a rough, violent person; a bully or criminal
a bold, daring act, often sung about by ballad sellers
the person who will inherit a throne or title
money paid or demanded to free a prisoner

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Good readers notice what a character does when he's in danger. In Chapter 5, two outlaws grab the boys. Watch Jemmy. Does he fight, does he try to trick them, or does he stay quiet? And think about why he makes that choice. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence about the outlaws. Look at the correct one first. Billy gets a capital letter, because it's a name. Commas go around the describing part in the middle: raw as a skinned ox. And a comma goes before and, because and joins two ideas. Tap the yellow parts to see each rule. Then pick Sentence A or B, and type it with capitals, commas, and a period.

mods.todo: Type the whole word in each box. Then tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: Today you'll build words from their parts. Remember, inter means between, and sub means under. Say each pair of parts out loud, then say them together as one word. Inter, rupt: interrupt. Hear how the parts snap together? Type the whole word in each box, then tap Check My Answers. Look at the little meaning next to each one. It tells you what you just built.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Here's a word from Chapter 5: ruffian. The prince calls Billy a clod and a ruffian. He's insulting him, so a ruffian must be someone rough and rude. Ruffian has no parts to help, so the sentence does the work. A ruffian is a rough, violent person, a bully. Now the other words in the word bank. An exploit is a bold, daring act. An heir is the person who will be king one day. And a ransom is money demanded to set a prisoner free. Fill in each sentence, then tap Check My Work.

mods.todo: Type and, but, or so in each blank. Tap Check My Answers. Then write a sentence that uses but.
mods.script: Today you'll do the joining yourself. Each pair has two short sentences. Glue them into one with and, but, or so. Ask yourself: am I adding an idea? Use and. Are the two ideas different, or surprising? Use but. Does the first thing cause the second? Use so. Read each one out loud with the word you picked. Then tap Check My Answers, and write your own sentence about Chapter 5 that uses but.

mods.todo: Find the vowel team in each word. Then tap the word to split it.
mods.script: Remember vowel teams? Two vowels side by side making one sound. Here's today's rule: when you split a word into syllables, never split the team. The team always stays together. Rain, bow. Sea, son. Look at each word, find the vowel team, and think about where the split goes. Then tap the word to check. The split goes between the syllables, never through the team.

Think about this before you read. When two outlaws grab the boys, the prince keeps telling them who he is. Jemmy tries to stop him without saying a word. Why would Jemmy want the prince to stay quiet? What might happen if outlaws find out they have a prince? Watch who keeps his head, and who keeps talking.

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read Ch. 5 in your book.
mods.script: Time to read Chapter 5. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. In this chapter, Jemmy jabs the prince with his elbow. Ask yourself why. Then watch the outlaw named Cutwater. He notices something on the saddle that changes everything. Stop at each question, think of your answer, and keep reading. After you read, try the King's Crest to see what Cutwater saw.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now show what you understood, in full sentences with details from the book. One, how does Jemmy know who Hold-Your-Nose Billy is, and what does that tell us about how famous Billy is? Two, when the prince says who he is, the outlaws don't bow. What do they do instead? Three, Jemmy jabbed the prince to keep him quiet. Was that the right thing to do? Use a detail to back up your answer. For a challenge, pick Scholar and add one more detail.

mods.script: You have a claim and a reason. Today you'll prove your reason with an example from the book. Clara's reason was, Prince Brat enjoys watching Jemmy get whipped. To prove it, she found a real moment. For example, in Chapter 2, the prince tells the tutor, ten whacks at least. Always name the chapter, so your reader can find it. Now write one example of your own. Start with, For example, in Chapter. Then copy it into your document.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: The outlaws grab them, and the prince shouts, “Don’t you know who I am!”
items.why: Shouting is not the same as courage. It puts both boys in danger.

items.t: Jemmy jabs the prince with his elbow to make him stop talking.
items.why: Jemmy thinks fast to keep them both safe.

items.t: Jemmy tells the outlaws that his friend’s father is only a rat-catcher.
items.why: He stays calm and tries a trick to protect them. That takes courage.
